hints: Focus on what changes down Group 17, the size and electronegativity of the halogen atom from Cl to Br to I.
Remember that boiling point depends on strength of London forces which grow with more electrons, while bond polarity depends on electronegativity difference.
Think about which C-X bond is longest and weakest, and how easily it breaks when a nucleophile attacks.
walkthrough:
**Check statement 1, bond polarity**

Think of polarity as tug of war for electrons. Chlorine is the most electronegative, iodine is the least.

Electronegativity: $\text{Cl} > \text{Br} > \text{I}$, so polarity $\text{C-Cl} > \text{C-Br} > \text{C-I}$. Statement 1 decreases, so it is false.

**Check statement 2, boiling point**

Boiling point for these similar molecules is controlled by London dispersion forces. From Cl to Br to I the molecule gets bigger with many more electrons.

More electrons means stronger temporary dipoles and stronger London forces, so more energy is needed to separate molecules: boiling point $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} < \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br} < \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{I}$. Statement 2 is true.

**Check statement 3, rate of nucleophilic substitution**

The slow, rate-determining step involves breaking the $\text{C-X}$ bond. A larger halogen gives a longer, weaker bond that breaks more easily.

Bond enthalpy: $\text{C-Cl} > \text{C-Br} > \text{C-I}$, so reactivity is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{I} > \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br} > \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$. Statement 3 steadily increases, so it is true.

**Combine the conclusions**

Only statements 2 and 3 show a steady increase from chloride to bromide to iodide. Statement 1 shows a steady decrease.

That combination of 2 and 3 only matches the correct option.

options.A: This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, but statement 1 is wrong because bond polarity decreases as electronegativity falls from Cl to I.
options.B: This option claims 1 and 2 only are correct. Statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect for the reason above, and it wrongly leaves out statement 3 which is correct because the weaker C-I bond reacts fastest.
options.C: This option claims 2 and 3 only are correct. This is right because boiling point increases with stronger London forces, and rate of nucleophilic substitution increases as the C-X bond gets weaker from Cl to I, while polarity decreases.
options.D: This option claims 1 only is correct. Statement 1 is false because the $\text{C-Cl}$ bond is most polar and the $\text{C-I}$ bond is least polar, so polarity does not increase from chloride to iodide.
